messages.content: You design amateur rockets that fly on certified commercial motors. Work through the design, check it with the tools, and give the final design as JSON inside <design> tags. Only report results the tools returned.
65,000 ft on one I205, single stage.

messages.reasoning_content:
1. Understand: apogee of 65,000 ft, which is 65000 * 0.3048 = 19,812 m (the wording is a target, so I treat it as about 19,800 m, within 5%). Motor is one I205 (fixed). Single stage (fixed). Landing speed, wind, rail and site are not stated, so 6 m/s, 2 m/s wind, a 1.5 m rail and sea level.
2. Feasibility: no-drag speed for 19,812 m is sqrt(2*9.81*19812) = 624 m/s, and a real rocket needs more impulse than that once drag is included. An I motor is only a few hundred newton-seconds. I need the I205's impulse and mass before I call the altitude impossible, but it already looks far out of reach for one I in a single stage.

2. Feasibility: the lookup returns the AeroTech HP-I205W, class I, only 346.4 N*s at 204.4 N average. The case is 29 mm, 0.305 m long, 0.315 kg, with a single 14 s delay. Even if the whole 346.4 N*s went into a 0.40 kg rocket with no drag, burnout speed would be about 346.4 / 0.40 = 866 m/s and the vacuum height 866^2 / (2*9.81) = 38,200 m. Drag at that speed on a real tube will take most of that away. 19,800 m is not plausible, but I will fly the lightest single-stage airframe I can so the shortfall is a measured one.
3. Size: guessed liftoff mass 0.45 kg. Thrust-to-weight = 204.4 / (0.45 * 9.81) = 46.3. Pad weight 0.45 * 9.81 = 4.41 N, rail acceleration (204.4 - 4.41) / 0.45 = 444 m/s^2, exit speed sqrt(2 * 444 * 1.5) = 36.5 m/s. Descent mass 0.45 - 0.188 = 0.26 kg. A 5 m/s chute needs 2 * 0.26 * 9.81 / (1.225 * 0.8 * 5^2) = 0.208 m^2, diameter sqrt(4 * 0.208 / 3.1416) = 0.51 m. I will use 0.55 m and open it at apogee, with the motor plugged, so a 14 s ejection does not cut the coast short.
4. Draft: 0.10 m polystyrene ogive on a 0.48 m cardboard tube, outer diameter 0.038 m, wall 0.8 mm. Mount 0.033 m outside, 0.32 m long, HP-I205W plugged. Three balsa fins, root 0.10 m, tip 0.040 m, span 0.055 m, sweep 0.050 m, 3 mm thick. Chute 0.55 m at apogee. Site defaults for wind and rail.
